narratives.Description: fix(scope): warn when a declaration added after activation lowers the evidence a clause requires
narratives.Overview:
1. Add one helper beside inferRequiredStrictAxes in packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts that returns an item's hidden axes: the axes inferred with the eight declaration fields ignored, minus the axes inferred as written. Do not copy the field list into another file.
2. In evaluateScopeProvenance, for each brief modified in the change set, read its merge-base copy through the same continuity and pre-move resolution the path fence uses (resolveMergeBaseBriefRead), so a head brief under completed/ or cancelled/ is compared with its pre-move copy. Do not change evaluateLegacyIntent or what legacy-intent-edit reports.
3. Warn for a head item when all three hold: (a) the resolved merge-base copy of the brief is under xbrief/active/; (b) the item is absent from that copy, or the value of any of the eight declaration fields differs from the base item, where items match by id and an item with no id matches by its position in the item tree; (c) the head item hides an axis that the base item does not hide, and an absent base item hides none.
4. Print one line for each such item through formatDeclaredRefusal on the extra-path warning channel (extraPathReport), naming the brief path, the item and the newly hidden axes. The exit code does not change, and the line is not counted as an intent-pin finding.
5. Add the row declaration-hides-axis to packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts with no mode (warn), remedy ["deft verify:scope-provenance"], and deferred "the fix is a brief edit in the same change (remove the added declaration, or record the evidence the clause requires); no printed command can make it for you; owned by #6591". Add its case to remedy-runs.test.ts in the same form as extra-path-not-admitted.
6. formatStrictAxisAdvisory takes the calling verb. At promote and activate it keeps the sentence that names x-directive/requires. At xbrief:preflight it prints the list and omits that sentence.
7. listStrictAxisRequirements also returns a row for an item with hidden axes, marked declared, with those axes. The count in the advisory's first line and the equality with the completion gate stay on items whose as-written axis set is not empty. The advisory prints declared rows after them, marked as declared.
8. Tests beside the changed sources, each on a brief with no intent pin. A line prints, exit 0, for: requires merge added to an item whose text infers deploy while the brief stays in active/; the same edit in the change that moves the brief to completed/; requires deploy added to "Deploy to staging and run the smoke test" (names smoke); a new item with requires merge and deploy text on a brief that is active on the base; and each of the seven alias fields in place of x-directive/requires. No line prints for: a lifecycle move with no declaration change; a declaration already on the base item; requires deploy added to deploy-only text; an edit that adds only x-directive/evidence; a title that gains "deploy" under an unchanged merge declaration; an alias swapped for another with the same hidden set; and a pending/ to active/ change that first writes the declaration.
9. Document the row in content/docs/scope-provenance.md: what it compares, that it warns only, that a declaration on the merge base is agent precommitment and not human authorization, and that the intent pin already refuses the same edit when a pin exists. Add a changelog fragment that says the row ships in warn mode.
10. Ship no new x-directive/requires value and no enforce mode for this row.

The proposed new value is not justified by the current baseline: `x-directive/requires: merge` already turns off text inference while admitting test or review evidence.

## F1 — blocks-the-design: the missing capability already exists

**Evidence.** At dispatch SHA `66d8171f5caaae7e5821e3f651fc1fec27873662`, [inference returns an empty axis set for merge-only declarations](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/66d8171f5caaae7e5821e3f651fc1fec27873662/packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts#L366-L385). [Suitability](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/66d8171f5caaae7e5821e3f651fc1fec27873662/packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts#L543-L559) requires a declaration **when the evidence kind is merge**; it does not require merge evidence whenever the declaration is merge. Every non-merge kind passes suitability when the axis set is empty.

I replayed the pinned `stampNamespacedEvidence` → `evaluateOneItem` functions on a pending `clause.1` titled “the `deploy` job is green”:

| Declaration | Evidence | Axes | Per-item result |
|---|---|---|---|
| absent | test | deploy | invalid |
| absent | review | deploy | invalid |
| merge | test | none | evidence |
| merge | review | none | evidence |

Pointers were `src/jobs.test.ts` and `docs/job-review.md`; neither was a commit SHA. The automatic [match-any stamper](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/66d8171f5caaae7e5821e3f651fc1fec27873662/packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts#L1057-L1075) also checks the inferred axes before choosing test/review from the artifact pointer.

**Failure mode.** Step 2 would add a second spelling for existing admission behavior, based on the false assertion that `requires: merge` demands a commit pointer. Its positive acceptance case would not establish a new capability.

**Disposition consequence.** Correct “What exists today” and the pain baseline before binding a new token. Census any remaining failure of the existing declared path. The real listing behavior is narrower: `listStrictAxisRequirements` omits the declared item (`[]`), so declaration visibility is a possible separate need, not proof that test/review admission is missing.

## F2 — sharpens-framing: declaration authority already has an intent-pin control

**Evidence.** [Item classification](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/66d8171f5caaae7e5821e3f651fc1fec27873662/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/known-machine.ts#L66-L83) excludes canonical evidence from intent, but does not exclude `x-directive/requires`. [Extraction](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/66d8171f5caaae7e5821e3f651fc1fec27873662/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/extract-intent.ts#L140-L187) retains that unknown key. A pinned-function replay of extraction and item comparison produced `intent-drift` when adding `requires: merge`, and no drift when adding only evidence. [Intent evaluation](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/66d8171f5caaae7e5821e3f651fc1fec27873662/packages/core/src/scope-provenance/intent-evaluate.ts#L148-L248) uses the base preimage, rejects same-change approval/preimage rewrites, and treats legacy intent edits as warnings.

**Failure mode.** Treating declarations as machine-written evidence would let an agent suppress a real deployment requirement without changing the compared intent. Conversely, “present at activation” alone does not establish human approval, and legacy warning behavior is not a universal refusal. An injected instruction to add a declaration is precisely an authority-changing intent edit, not ordinary evidence capture.

**Disposition consequence.** Inventory and preserve this existing control before adding a parallel approval mechanism. If a new value remains necessary, bind its authority to the approved declaration/intent and test subsequent changes through the existing provenance path. State the legacy/unpinned limit explicitly; do not claim that a pure inference function authenticates its caller or that reviewer attention closes the gap.

## F3 — sharpens-framing: an empty refusal census needs an observation boundary

**Evidence.** The body describes the earlier 0-of-114 result as an axis delta after removing code content from stored plan items. That is a different measurement from post-#6270 consumer refusal history. I have not reproduced or disputed that earlier count. Reworded and abandoned attempts can disappear from a current-brief scan.

**Failure mode.** No accessible refusal records could be reported as zero consumer pain, allowing the empty-census branch to claim more than was observed.

**Disposition consequence.** Name the repositories, versions/time window, and refusal/history sources actually covered. Distinguish zero observed cases from unavailable history, and test whether current `requires: merge` plus test/review serves each observed case. A bounded empty result can support no implementation for that corpus; it cannot establish universal absence or, by itself, relief of the text-inference behavior in P1. No new telemetry system is needed for this decision.

**Road not taken.** A differently named non-strict token could communicate intent more clearly and could deliberately exclude merge evidence. That would be a distinct semantic contract worth considering if the census establishes that need. Neither distinction is required by the present positive AC, so I prefer correcting the baseline before expanding the value set.

**Verification limits.** Source verification used dispatch-SHA-pinned reads; all three supplied blob hashes matched. Checks used Node type stripping on complete pinned function slices, with assertions for the cases above and explicit-strict-axis precedence. These were isolated function checks, not an end-to-end `scope:complete` run. The checkout runtime pin was absent, so the read-only session/routing commands could not run. Round 1 critic, fresh seat, open critique. Input: issue body and comments through 6965320207. Tree: `66d8171f5caaae7e5821e3f651fc1fec27873662`. Verification: pin-read with `git show <sha>:<path>`, plus scratch runs of the pinned source outside the dest (`git archive` of the dispatch SHA into `/tmp`, Node 24 `--experimental-transform-types`, `parse5` and `typescript` stubbed, no dest writes). The three inventory blob ids match the envelope.

## Summary

The proposal rests on "There is no declaration that says test or review evidence is enough for this clause". At the dispatch SHA, `x-directive/requires: merge` is already that declaration. It turns the text match off, `scope:stamp-evidence` stamps `kind: test` on the item, and `scope:complete` accepts `kind: test` or `kind: review`. So step 2's first acceptance criterion already holds with `merge` in place of the new value. The "who may write" question is not about a future value: it is a live hole on the existing key, and the census cannot settle it either way.

## Findings

### F1. `requires: merge` already admits test and review evidence (`blocks-the-design`)

Evidence, run at the pin on the clause text "the `deploy` job is green":

| Item | `inferRequiredStrictAxes` | stamp | `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` |
|---|---|---|---|
| no declaration, `kind: test` | `[deploy]` | skipped `strict-axis` | invalid |
| `requires: merge`, `kind: test` | `[]` | `stampMatchAnyFileEvidence` and `stampDeclaredTestEvidence` both stamp `kind: test` | evidence, ok |
| `requires: merge`, `kind: review` (pointer `docs/x.md`) | `[]` | n/a | evidence, ok |

Cause: in `isEvidenceKindSuitable`, `mergeDeclared` only gates `kind: merge`. With an empty axis set every other kind returns true. The body's line "then the item needs `kind: merge` evidence with a commit SHA" is false.

What `merge` does cost, measured at the pin:
- `evaluateInPrCompletionInputs` (`scope/lands-with-product.ts`) refuses `scope:complete --in-pr` for any item that declares merge ("c1 declares the merge requirement", #6277).
- `listStrictAxisRequirements` drops the item, so the #6272 listing shows it as absent.
- The token says "merge" when the evidence is a test.

Failure mode: a step-2 build passes every listed acceptance criterion while the only behaviour that moves is in-PR completion. Or the census closes the issue against a wrong baseline ("merge needs a SHA").

Disposition consequence: rewrite "What exists today" and the step-2 trigger. A new value can only buy in-PR completion, the listing, and an honest label over `merge`. Name those as the goal, or drop step 2. The listing gap can be fixed for `merge` alone.

### F2. The who-may-write hole is live today, so a census-empty close leaves it open (`blocks-the-design`)

Evidence:
- `inferRequiredStrictAxes` reads the declaration from the current item bytes. Nothing checks when or by whom it was written. That holds for the canonical key and its seven dual-read aliases (`readExplicitAcceptanceRequirementFields`).
- Probe of `evaluateIntentForXbrief` with no approved-scope mint (the normal case after #4956): adding `x-directive/requires: merge` to an active item after activation returns two `legacy-intent-edit` findings, both `warnOnly: true`. A hand-added disposition gets the same result. With a mint, the same edit gives non-warn findings (code read, not run).
- The gate probe in F1 used `recorded_by: agent-x`. Nothing on the evidence path asks for human origin.

Failure mode: a `drive-to: merge-ready` worker whose `scope:complete` refuses on a real deploy claim adds `"x-directive/requires": "merge"` to the item, runs `scope:stamp-evidence`, and completes. ## Summary

An agent can switch off a runtime-evidence requirement on a brief that is already active, and the framework says little or nothing about it.

`inferRequiredStrictAxes` (`packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts`) gives a clause such as "Deploy to staging and confirm the site serves the new build" a deploy axis, so `scope:complete` refuses test evidence for it. If the item then gains `"x-directive/requires": "merge"`, the axis set becomes empty and `kind: test` or `kind: review` evidence is accepted. Nothing checks who added the declaration or when.

This issue makes that edit visible, in warn mode, and stops the framework from suggesting it. It adds no new `x-directive/requires` value.

## Recut note

The first version of this issue said that `requires: merge` needs `kind: merge` evidence with a commit SHA, and proposed a new non-strict value. That was wrong. Round-1 critics 6965408516 and 6965496784 showed that a merge declaration already turns the text match off and admits test or review evidence. The clause that only names a job or workflow (#6301 P1) is therefore already served: the author declares `x-directive/requires: merge` before activation. What remains is the authority gap below.

## Evidence

Measured at `66d8171f5caaae7e5821e3f651fc1fec27873662`.

Real `evaluateScopeProvenance` in disposable git repositories, on a brief with the clause above and no intent pin:

| Change against the merge base | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Add test evidence only; brief stays in `active/` | clean |
| Add `requires: merge` and test evidence; brief stays in `active/` | exit 0, two warn-only `legacy-intent-edit` findings |
| Move the brief to `completed/` only | clean |
| Move to `completed/` and add `requires: merge` and test evidence | clean: exit 0, no finding, no warning |

- The last row is a blind spot. `evaluateLegacyIntent` reads the merge-base copy at the head path. After a lifecycle move that path does not exist on the base, so the comparison returns nothing. The path fence in the same file already resolves the pre-move path.
- `scope:complete --in-pr` refuses an item that declares merge (#6277), so a merge-declared brief completes through the later lifecycle move, which is the blind spot.
- With an intent pin, the same edit returns hard `intent-drift` and `unclassified-key` findings (function-level probe of `evaluateIntentForXbrief`).
- `xbrief:preflight` prints the #6272 advisory on an active brief: "reword the clause or declare x-directive/requires (merge or one axis) on the item". That tells the worker to make this edit.
- `listStrictAxisRequirements` lists only items with a non-empty axis set, so an item whose declaration hides a text axis is absent from the listing.
- Census of all briefs at the pin: 1,951 of 10,554 plan items declare merge, in 139 briefs, 131 of which declare it on every top-level item. 14 items have a declaration that hides a text-inferred axis (13 completed on `kind: merge`, 1 on a disposition). Consumer refusals are not observable from this repository.

## Constraints

- Warn-first (#6281): a new default refusal is declared in the refusal table (`packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts`) and ships in `warn` mode for at least one release. This issue ships `warn` only. A move to `enforce` is a later release with its own CHANGELOG entry and is not part of this issue.
- No scope ceremony after proceed (#4956): the remedy must not require an extra brief-only PR.
- `legacy-intent-edit` stays advisory (#5057). This issue adds one narrow declared row; it does not turn intent edits in general into refusals.
- A declaration that is present on the merge base is agent precommitment reviewed at activation, not human authorization (`content/docs/scope-provenance.md`). This issue does not claim otherwise and does not address blanket declarations made before activation.

## Proposal

1. **Close the blind spot.** When the head brief is under `completed/` or `cancelled/` and its path is absent on the merge base, the unpinned intent comparison reads the pre-move brief the same way the path fence does.
2. **One declared warn row.** For each head item, compute the hidden axes: the axes its text infers with the declaration fields removed, minus the axes it infers as written. When an item hides an axis that the same item (matched by id) did not hide on the merge base, or the item is new, print one declared refusal line in `warn` mode that names the item, the hidden axes, and a remedy that runs as printed. All eight declaration fields count (`x-directive/requires` and its aliases).
3. **Advisory by verb.** At promote and activate the #6272 advisory keeps "declare x-directive/requires". At `xbrief:preflight` on an active brief it does not suggest adding a declaration.
4. **Listing.** `listStrictAxisRequirements` and the advisory show an item whose declaration hides a text axis as declared, with the hidden axes, not as absent.

## Out of scope

- A new `x-directive/requires` value.
- Any inference from clause text (#6301 is the record).
- `enforce` mode for the new row.
- Human-origin records for declarations made before activation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an active brief with no intent pin whose item text infers deploy, when the head adds `x-directive/requires: merge` to that item and the brief stays in `active/`, then `verify:scope-provenance` prints the declared warn line naming the item and `deploy`, and exits 0.
- Given the same edit made in the change that moves the brief to `completed/`, then the same warn line prints.
- Given a lifecycle move with no declaration change, then no warn line prints.
- Given a declaration that is already on the merge-base copy of the item, then no warn line prints.
- Given an edit that raises the requirement (adds `x-directive/requires: deploy`), then no warn line prints.
- Given an edit that adds only `x-directive/evidence`, then no warn line prints.
- Given each of the seven alias fields in place of `x-directive/requires`, then the warn line prints.
- The new row is in the refusal table with mode `warn`, prints through the one helper with its gate id, and its remedy passes the remedy test.
- Given an active brief, when `xbrief:preflight` prints the strict-axis advisory, then the text does not tell the reader to declare `x-directive/requires`.
- Given an item with `x-directive/requires: merge` whose text infers deploy, then `listStrictAxisRequirements` returns a row for it marked declared with `deploy` as hidden.
- Tests live beside the changed sources and pass under Vitest.

Refs #6301, #6270, #6272, #6277, #6281, #5105, #5057, #4956, #2944.
